title: Which sea gets the rain?
hook: Rain falls on an island between two seas. Which one does it end up in?

knows: rivers run downhill to the sea
doesNotKnow: that a drainage divide, not distance, decides which sea gets the rain
that a divide near one coast sends most of the land to the far one

misconception: Rain that falls on land flows to the nearest sea.
objective: The learner can explain that rain follows the slope to whichever sea lies on its side of the drainage divide, so a divide near the west coast sends most of the land (here about four fifths) to the far, east sea.

claims.text: A drop at the dot, 55 km from the west sea and 150 km from the east sea, runs downhill to the east sea; a drop west of the ridge runs to the west sea.
claims.source: Made-up island, 40 x 24 squares of 5 km, ridge at x = 7 +/- 1.5 plus noise from mulberry32 seed 7 (seed set in the brief before running, disclosed here). Priority-flood pit filling (Barnes, Lehman and Mulla 2014), then D8 steepest descent (O'Callaghan and Mark 1984). Dot at square (10, 12): 11 squares (55 km) from the west sea, 30 squares (150 km) from the east sea; ends east. Drop at (5, 12) ends west. src/demos/geography/which-sea-gets-the-rain/model.ts, a port of section `watershed` in company/domains/briefs/checks/geography-wave-j.mjs; builder re-ran both and they agree (764 east, 79.6%).
claims.note: Simulation re-run: node ran model.ts itself (type-stripped copy). Drop at (10, 12) ends east after 30 squares; drop at (5, 12) ends west. 55 km = 11 x 5 and 150 km = 30 x 5. Identical to section 'watershed' of company/domains/briefs/checks/geography-wave-j.mjs (its mulberry32 is written differently but is equivalent). artifacts/fact-check-wave-j/wj-econ-phys-math-geo/geo/.

claims.text: About four fifths of the island (80%) drains east.
claims.source: Same model: 764 of 960 squares (79.6%, shown rounded to 80%) end in the east sea; 284 squares nearer the west coast still drain east. Section `watershed` of company/domains/briefs/checks/geography-wave-j.mjs; model.ts eastCount.
claims.note: Simulation re-run: 764 of 960 east (79.6%, shown 80%), 284 nearer the west coast still drain east. The divide sits at x = 7-9 in every row, with no east square west of a west square in any row.

claims.text: Water follows the slope, and the ridge is a divide: every drop on one side ends in one sea, every drop on the other side in the other.
claims.source: Definition of a drainage divide (the boundary between land draining to different outlets). True by construction in the model: each square has exactly one outlet, and the drawn divide is the set of square edges between squares with different outlets (Demo.tsx divideSegs).
claims.note: Definition, true by construction: every square has one outlet, and divideSegs are the edges between squares with different outlets.

claims.source: Scope statement on the stage caption: the island is a toy; no real river or basin is named (the kit has no river data).
claims.note: Convention: the stage caption, and KM = 5.

claims.text: Recall: a ridge 20 km from a country's west coast means most of its rain probably reaches the east coast ('everything east of the ridge drains east, and that is most of the land').
claims.source: Unrecorded claim found by the fact-checker in meta.json recall (question and why). Rests on c3 plus an unstated assumption that the country is much wider than 40 km.
claims.note: Recorded by the fact-checker as an unrecorded learner-facing claim (so I do not verify it myself). It holds only if the country is wider than twice the ridge's distance from the coast; the recall never says so. Fix for demo-builder: state a width (for example 'a country 300 km wide'), then a different checker verifies it.

recall.question: A ridge runs 20 km from a country's west coast. Most of its rain probably reaches which coast?
recall.why: The divide, not the distance, decides: everything east of the ridge drains east, and that is most of the land.
